title: Frozen-code-ceiling probe: ridge vs diagonal ridge vs kNN on the sealed SPM codes
registered_in: analysis/RESEARCH_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_v24.md section 7 Phase D (M176a) / section 12 dispatch entry (17 Aug 2026)
question: How much accuracy can ANY non-trained head extract from the sealed SPM codes at the C4 138k level?

interpretation_registered_before_running.a: kNN roughly ties ridge: no easy head-side accuracy is left in the codes for these head families — L1 (the code ceiling) is confirmed for this family.
interpretation_registered_before_running.b: diagonal << ridge and kNN ~ ridge: linear cross-feature structure is load-bearing; the ceiling is the full ridge's, not the code's.
interpretation_registered_before_running.c: kNN >> ridge: the codes hold non-linear structure a better head could exploit — contradicts M150's trained-head collapse; M176c priority rises.
interpretation_registered_before_running.scope_note: measuring stick, not a win/loss gate; the probe covers two alternative head families (diagonal-ridge, kNN) and is not a bound on all possible heads.

diagonal.note: per-column independent weights over the SAME standardised features the ridge sees (including the bias column); float64 accumulation, cast at the boundary

knn.metric: cosine on the power-normalised codes (signed sqrt + per-row L2)
knn.note: exact nearest neighbours via chunked matmul; top-k majority vote
